name: Spider scalar
summary: A spider without any legs is the scalar 1 + $e^{iα}$.
description:
A Z-spider (or X-spider) with phase α and no inputs or outputs is the scalar $1+e^{i\alpha}$: it is the sum of the two terms $\langle 0|0\rangle$ and $e^{i\alpha}\langle 1|1\rangle$ of the spider.

Two special cases are particularly important: a phase-free spider without legs is the scalar 2, and a spider with phase π and no legs is the scalar **0**. A diagram containing such a zero scalar is zero, and complete calculi need a rule (the *zero rule*) that lets such diagrams be brought to a normal form.

Together with the [two-spider scalars](../scalar-state-effect/) and the [1/√2 scalar](../scalar-inverse-sqrt2/), every complex number can be written as a scalar ZX-diagram.
